subject: general
question: The average marks of a student in six subjects was initially 110. After re-evaluation, in one subject the marks obtained was reduced from 148 to 112, while in the rest of the subjects the marks remained unchanged. What is the new average marks?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial average = 110 for 6 subjects

⇒ Initial total = 110 × 6 = 660

⇒ Marks reduced by = 148 − 112 = 36

⇒ New total = 660 − 36 = 624

⇒ New average = 624 ÷ 6 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of subjects = 6

Initial average marks = 110

Marks reduced from 148 to 112

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Marks ÷ Number of Subjects

 660 Marks 
• -36 624 Marks 6 Subjects 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial total marks = 110 × 6

⇒ = 660

⇒ Reduction in marks = 148 − 112

⇒ = 36

⇒ New total marks = 660 − 36

⇒ = 624

⇒ New average = 624 ÷ 6

⇒ = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of Observations.

Change in Average

If one value changes by d, then the average changes by d ÷ n, where n is the number of observations.

Total from Average

Total Sum = Average × Number of Observations.

Re-evaluation Problems

First find the increase or decrease in marks, adjust the total, then calculate the new average.
